strongest_comparator: The pure inverse-square Bessel mode already has logarithmic phase winding and a geometric sequence for any fixed real phase. The previous full-coupling result proves minimal-domain injectivity and a one-dimensional adjoint cokernel but does not determine the maximal homogeneous mode or its trace.
hardest_step: Control the actual coupled mode in the scaled maximal graph norm so its boundary trace, not merely its H norm, has a relative O(gamma^-2) error. Distinguish the maximal homogeneous vector using V from the source-adjoint vector using V^*.
new_consequence: The actual auxiliary thermal maximal kernel is one dimensional, exactly one reflecting phase is resonant at each sufficiently high frequency, and the resonant phase has O(gamma^-2) error from the Bessel phase. Other phases have an explicit inverse; the resonant range equals the minimal range. Thermal phases approach every target without implying a fixed-phase Matsubara zero.
conditional_continuous_theorem: If the actual causal elimination extends as a real operator-norm continuous uniformly bounded remainder on the same strong graph realization at every sufficiently large real gamma, each fixed phase has a sequence of auxiliary homogeneous zeros with asymptotic frequency ratio exp(pi/k). This hypothesis is not proved for the actual charged response.
scope_boundary: No physical gravitational phase, exact fixed-phase Matsubara resonance, continuous causal extension, charged Lorentzian instability, effective-theory frequency window, nonlinear geometry or physical stability theorem is certified.
regulator_contract: Keep original state, action, clock, flux, angular response, residual contacts and existing auxiliary shape realization. No finite term, boundary prescription, source projection or order reduction is adopted.
verification_scope: Exact boundary dilation and Green pairing, a nonnormal finite row model of the algebra, Bessel trace extraction at three cutoffs and two precisions, and an exactly solvable bounded constant-potential continuous comparator. No charged-kernel approximation or benchmark calibration is inferred.
